Peter — **President Trump promised not to cut Medicaid. But this week, Republicans in Washington DC voted for a bill that likely rips away health insurance from 630,000 hard-working North Carolinians. This will especially hurt our rural areas like western NC.** In an overwhelming 2023 bipartisan vote, we finally expanded Medicaid in North Carolina after a decade of fighting for it. It is a huge success so far — hundreds of thousands of working people can get the health care they need. We enrolled twice as many people as we thought possible during the first year because there was so much demand for quality health care. It was the right thing to do — for our economy, for rural hospitals, for mental health, and more. The very premise is outrageous: Gutting Medicaid to fund tax cuts for billionaires. Stripping health care access from the people who need it most, so that the wealthy can pay even _less_ of their fair share. **Peter, many Republican politicians, including Donald Trump, promised they wouldn’t touch Medicaid. By Illinois Review

On Thursday, DuPage County Sheriff James Mendrick announced that he won’t be seeking a third-term as the county’s top law enforcement official – and instead, will be consolidating his efforts to run for governor of Illinois.

“Sheriff Mendrick is running for Governor of Illinois!!!,” said a Facebook post on James Mendrick DuPage County Sheriff. Mendrick then noted that it was not an easy decision, but the right one.

“My family and I have decided that we want our State back. We don’t like being fearful of crime that is randomly occurring now in our streets, homes and our retail stores due to soft on crime legislation. We don’t want to move out of Illinois like so much of our population. We really don’t. We love this state. That’s why I’ve decided to run for the Office of Governor of Illinois.”

Senator Anderson Legislative Newsletter
---

* * *
---
As Oregon’s families continue to navigate the rising cost of childcare, I recognize the hard work that parents put in everyday to balance work and family life. Ensuring that parents can find high-quality, affordable childcare is a priority that deserves thoughtful and practical solutions.
In the Oregon legislature, we believe in empowering parents and communities, not burdening them with unnecessary regulations. Our approach to improving childcare is rooted in the belief that families know best when it comes to caring for their children, and the government’s role should be to support, not control their choices.
Here is what we are focusing on:
**Prioritizing Families and Flexibility**
A strong family is the backbone of our communities, and every parent should have the freedom to choose the childcare solution that works best for them—whether it’s through traditional daycare, in-home care, or family- based childcare. This is why I support policies that provide tax relief and support for families who want to make the most of their childcare options.
**Promoting Affordability**
Childcare is expensive and hard to find; no family should be forced to choose between working to support their household or caring for their children. Through initiatives such as expanding the Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit, we can help reduce the financial burden and ensure that families can keep more of their hard-earned money. I am also exploring solutions which can lead to a larger supply of facilities and more affordable and flexible childcare options.
**Strengthening the Workforce and Supporting Providers**
Childcare workers are a vital part of our economy and communities. We must ensure that they have the resources and flexibility they need to offer high-quality services, while also maintaining the freedom to operate and innovate. By supporting workforce development initiatives and providing tax incentives for businesses that invest in childcare options for their employees, we can help boost childcare availability and job opportunities in Oregon.
Together, we can create a childcare system that helps families succeed while ensuring that our children have the best start in life. I will continue working to support policies that empower parents, protect families, and strengthen our communities.
Thank you for your continued trust and support. Let’s work together to make our district an even better place for families to grow and thrive.
* * *

Speaking on the senate floor regarding childcare. "A child's future doesn't begin in the classroom; it begins in the earliest years, with access to safe, reliable care. Supporting working parents and increasing childcare availability isn't just an economic issue- it's an investment in the well-being of our children."

Last Newsletter I touched on the process of how a bill becomes a law through the legislative process. This week I thought it would be interesting to highlight the difference between the State and Federal Government.
The Supremacy Clause is a key element to the United States Constitution. Found in Article VI, Clause 2 states that the Constitution, along with federal laws and treaties is the "supreme law of the land." This means that if a state law conflicts with the federal law, federal law takes precedence. In other words, when there is a clash between state and federal authority, the federal government's decisions, policies and laws will override those of individual states.
This clause helps maintain a unified legal framework across the entire country, ensuring that the national government has the ultimate authority in matters that concern the entire nation. The Supremacy Clause plays a crucial role in upholding the balance of power between state and federal governments and preventing legal conflicts from undermining the country's system of governance.
* * *
---
---
The 10th Amendment of the United State Constitution is part of the Bill of Rights and states: "The powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution, nor prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States respectively, or to the people."
In simple terms, it emphasized that any power not specifically given to the federal government by the Constitution is left to the states or to the people. This amendment highlights the principle of federalism, which is the division of power between the national and state governments. It serves as a reminder that the federal government's authority is limited to what is written in the Constitution, and all other powers remain with the states or the people themselves.
The 10th Amendment is important because it protects the rights of states and individuals by ensuring that the federal government doesn't overstep its constitutional boundaries. It's a critical safeguard for preserving the balance of power in the United States.
* * *
---
---
While the federal government focuses on issues that impact the nation as a whole, states have the authority to govern local issues, which allows for diversity and flexibility across the country. This system of checks and balances ensures that power is distributed, preventing any one level of government from being too powerful.
* * *

Here are some bills I am sponsoring that are related to Early Childhood Education:
[SB 439](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Folis.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fliz%2F2025R1%2FMeasures%2FOverview%2FSB439/1/0101019548892015-1403db39-e562-4654-815e-bf5d18ab4212-000000/xBxGHMsbVFwdOUZipkJM7vRB2tr8f_qoadnU-EAz_-w=394)\- Says that building a childcare center in a place that provides affordable housing does not mean that a person building the whole place must pay prevailing wage, but building the childcare center itself does require paying prevailing wage for labor.
[SB 561- ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Folis.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fliz%2F2025R1%2FMeasures%2FOverview%2FSB561/1/0101019548892015-1403db39-e562-4654-815e-bf5d18ab4212-000000/SQ_W47cQdX1emxQ9qRGRamOzfmsm8SPbPVMbORG75Vc=394)Creates an Oregon personal income tax subtraction for childcare expenses paid by a taxpayer during the tax year. Applies to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, and before January 1, 2031.
[SB 567- ](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Folis.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fliz%2F2025R1%2FMeasures%2FOverview%2FSB567/1/0101019548892015-1403db39-e562-4654-815e-bf5d18ab4212-000000/oNoxiLuPHHvn4EdAW-3i8Ydum3aeCJ3-Ve4QI3KznA8=394)The Act would create an incentive program for childcare. It directs the Department of Early Learning and Care to establish and implement a childcare provider incentive program. It establishes the Child Care Provider Incentive Fund.
[SB 962-](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Folis.oregonlegislature.gov%2Fliz%2F2025R1%2FMeasures%2FOverview%2FSB962/1/0101019548892015-1403db39-e562-4654-815e-bf5d18ab4212-000000/OQTY-vLHfRvTf66QhiHuXeRqzLyK-HmwL62UZCphhmA=394)Directs the Department of Early Learning and Care to administer a grant program to award moneys to tenants to update dwellings for use as a family childcare home.

**Oregon House, Senate Republicans outline education priorities, legislation this session** \- Read the KTVZ 21 article [HERE](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fktvz.com%2Fnews%2Foregon-northwest%2F2025%2F02%2F20%2Foregon-house-republicans-outline-education-priorities-legislation-this-session%2F/1/0101019548892015-1403db39-e562-4654-815e-bf5d18ab4212-000000/g6Ody1rwDULNiAsSp_fJATyQkZeQ5_RvDeerSZ7oKmI=394).

* * *
---
On January 31st, 2025, the residents of Surfside Village CO-OP, Nye Beach in Newport became resident owned!
Oregon legislation requires that when a park is put up for sale, the residents are given the opportunity to purchase the property first. Surfside Village was first put up for sale in 2015, however the owners and the committee of residents were unable to come to an agreeable purchase price, they were advised to wait and see if they could purchase again in the future. When the property was put up for sale again in 2024, they worked with Casa of Oregon for over ten months to make this possible.
There are currently 28 Resident Owned Communities (ROC) in Oregon. Unlike traditional manufactured home communities, ROCs are not subject to market-based rent increases and there is no profit margin in monthly site fees. This cooperative ownership gives homeowners the ability to control costs, improve facilities and make their own rules while providing the peace of mind of land ownership.
* * *
---
* * *
---
For many children in our communities, access to quality early education can make all the difference in their academic journey and beyond. Head Start, a national program focused on early childhood education, health and family well-being, serves as a lifeline for those who might otherwise face challengers before they even begin their formal education. By providing a solid foundation in a child’s early year, Head Start doesn’t prepare them for school- it prepares them for life.
Kidco Head Start started over 60 years ago in Sweet Home and since then has expanded to serve around 450 families in 28 classrooms at 12 different sites and locations throughout Linn and Benton Counties. The Philomath location, which is in Senate District 5, currently serves 17 families in the area. Kidco Head Start/ Early Head Start is a free infant/ toddler and preschool program.
The infant/ toddler program serves pregnant mothers and their children to 36 months of age. Kidco is the only provider licensed for Early Head Start in Linn-Benton Counties. The preschool program serves children who turn three or four years old.
One of the most important goals that Kidco has is to help children become confident and secure learners. The philosophy behind their curriculum is that young children learn best by doing, supported by responsive, caring and knowledgeable adults. That can be seen firsthand when you step foot in their buildings. The educators at Kidco believe in the importance of play. Their classroom extends to the playground and there is no screen time when students are in the building. The children in the classroom go outside and play every single day they are at the facility- weather permitting. All the activities they plan, organization, selection of materials, and how they interact with the children, are all designed to give each child a successful transition into kindergarten.
All the staff that my Office Manager Sam talked to while she visited the facility last week had been previous families. They are all extremely passionate about their jobs and the gifts they have been given. Head Start doesn’t just help the children, but their families as well. There are so many programs offered for parents including financial wellness, mental health support and extra supports offered directly to the child and family through an Interagency Committee.
There are many success stories that come out of Head Start. The children and families are given the tools to set themselves up for generational successes. In conclusion, Head Start continues to play a vital role in providing children with the early education and support they need to succeed in school and beyond. By fostering a strong foundation in academic skills, social development, and emotional well-being, Head Start helps level the playing field for children, setting them on a path toward lifelong success. As we move forward it is crucial to ensuring that every child can thrive from the very beginning of their educational journey.
Learn more about Kidco and what they do [HERE](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.kidcoheadstart.org%2F/1/0101019548892015-1403db39-e562-4654-815e-bf5d18ab4212-000000/rpH8FalPD1wrAUa15mGBtIF5Cc5gfYCmpA4Y3NRp3io=394)

clean_body: Senator Anderson Legislative Newsletter | | | "View Online" ---|--- | As Oregon’s families continue to navigate the rising cost of childcare, I recognize the hard work that parents put in everyday to balance work and family life. Ensuring that parents can find high-quality, affordable childcare is a priority that deserves thoughtful and practical solutions. In the Oregon legislature, we believe in empowering parents and communities, not burdening them with unnecessary regulations. Our approach to improving childcare is rooted in the belief that families know best when it comes to caring for their children, and the government’s role should be to support, not control their choices. Here is what we are focusing on: Prioritizing Families and Flexibility A strong family is the backbone of our communities, and every parent should have the freedom to choose the childcare solution that works best for them—whether it’s through traditional daycare, in-home care, or family- based childcare. This is why I support policies that provide tax relief and support for families who want to make the most of their childcare options. Promoting Affordability Childcare is expensive and hard to find; no family should be forced to choose between working to support their household or caring for their children. Through initiatives such as expanding the Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit, we can help reduce the financial burden and ensure that families can keep more of their hard-earned money. I am also exploring solutions which can lead to a larger supply of facilities and more affordable and flexible childcare options. Strengthening the Workforce and Supporting Providers Childcare workers are a vital part of our economy and communities. We must ensure that they have the resources and flexibility they need to offer high-quality services, while also maintaining the freedom to operate and innovate. By supporting workforce development initiatives and providing tax incentives for businesses that invest in childcare options for their employees, we can help boost childcare availability and job opportunities in Oregon. Together, we can create a childcare system that helps families succeed while ensuring that our children have the best start in life. I will continue working to support policies that empower parents, protect families, and strengthen our communities. Thank you for your continued trust and support. Let’s work together to make our district an even better place for families to grow and thrive. Speaking on the senate floor regarding childcare. "A child's future doesn't begin in the classroom; it begins in the earliest years, with access to safe, reliable care. Supporting working parents and increasing childcare availability isn't just an economic issue- it's an investment in the well-being of our children." The event is also scheduled to be live streamed via Zoom: "" Last Newsletter I touched on the process of how a bill becomes a law through the legislative process. This week I thought it would be interesting to highlight the difference between the State and Federal Government. The Supremacy Clause is a key element to the United States Constitution. Found in Article VI, Clause 2 states that the Constitution, along with federal laws and treaties is the "supreme law of the land." This means that if a state law conflicts with the federal law, federal law takes precedence. In other words, when there is a clash between state and federal authority, the federal government's decisions, policies and laws will override those of individual states. This clause helps maintain a unified legal framework across the entire country, ensuring that the national government has the ultimate authority in matters that concern the entire nation. The Supremacy Clause plays a crucial role in upholding the balance of power between state and federal governments and preventing legal conflicts from undermining the country's system of governance. The 10th Amendment of the United State Constitution is part of the Bill of Rights and states: "The powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution, nor prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States respectively, or to the people." In simple terms, it emphasized that any power not specifically given to the federal government by the Constitution is left to the states or to the people. This amendment highlights the principle of federalism, which is the division of power between the national and state governments. It serves as a reminder that the federal government's authority is limited to what is written in the Constitution, and all other powers remain with the states or the people themselves. The 10th Amendment is important because it protects the rights of states and individuals by ensuring that the federal government doesn't overstep its constitutional boundaries. It's a critical safeguard for preserving the balance of power in the United States. While the federal government focuses on issues that impact the nation as a whole, states have the authority to govern local issues, which allows for diversity and flexibility across the country. This system of checks and balances ensures that power is distributed, preventing any one level of government from being too powerful. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/f36d3979-ea69-4f61-877d-56b5efb84cd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Since the day he descended an escalator to upend American politics, President Donald Trump has consistently delighted his supporters and confounded his critics. Seemingly on separate planets, these two groups hear the same pronouncements and emerge with radically different interpretations of what Trump said and what it might mean. During Trump's first term, an adage emerged to explain this dynamic: _Trump 's supporters take him seriously but not literally, while his detractors take him literally but not seriously._
Trump's recent foreign policy statements are perfect examples: Invade Panama? Annex Canada? [Buy Greenland](https://substack.com/redirect/905b53a7-0c3d-445b-9d81-7304f0c21cb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)?
Taking him literally, Trump's critics believe he is hellbent on invading our allies. Described by some supporters as "[Trump Derangement Syndrome](https://substack.com/redirect/eb4db2ee-fad1-47f8-8021-2bb878a07cf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," the inability of these critics to unemotionally evaluate the President's words inevitably leads to an incomplete interpretation of his intentions or likely actions. The conclusion: Trump is a madman without method. Literally, but not seriously.
> **Trump 's supporters take him seriously but not literally, while his detractors take him literally but not seriously.**
Trump's supporters, on the other hand, take such statements with a grain of salt, believing they are just opening gambits. They shrug off the suggestion America would invade a NATO ally or annex a neighbor to add another star to the flag. They don't believe Trump will invade [Greenland](https://substack.com/redirect/905b53a7-0c3d-445b-9d81-7304f0c21cb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but they grasp the island is vitally important to U.S. national and economic security. Looking past the madness, they detect a method - one in which the president makes bold statements out-of-the-gate, gaining advantage through surprise. Back during his days as a real estate developer, he was notorious for opening negotiations by threatening to sue everyone involved. Seriously, but not literally.
Behind the bombastic rhetoric, the United States may actually be telegraphing a coherent foreign policy, whether intentional or not. Whether it's Panama, Greenland, Ukraine, or even the signature issue of illegal immigration, these dots connect to reveal a foreign policy that is increasingly focused on the Western Hemisphere--a 21st century version of the[ Monroe Doctrine](https://substack.com/redirect/6bc0e76e-4904-4dec-af07-bf07b304f607?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The emerging U.S. foreign policy, best captured by the "America First" slogan, is focused on keeping our adversaries out of our neighborhood.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..vrWpIez0oFfC9aiGNYxjctYjMirR_W6Tf9IGLXmvdzM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=157958208)
Greenland and Panama are perfect examples. Not only are vital U.S. interests involved, but China has been trying to make inroads with both. Let's not forget that China controls ports at both entrances/exits to the Panama Canal and offered to buy an old naval base in Greenland. America's foreign policy, it appears, is telling our adversaries that our hemisphere is off limits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/98809aee-4db8-4447-855d-3c57fe6b30dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [https://www.history.com/topics/19th-century/monroe-doctrine](https://substack.com/redirect/6bc0e76e-4904-4dec-af07-bf07b304f607?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Americans are increasingly skeptical of foreign interventionism and political leadership now reflects this sentiment. Ukraine is a case in point. With each passing day, we seem to be approaching a consensus that Russia is Europe's problem...and if Europeans were truly worried about the threat, they would spend more on defense instead of expecting American protection while funding lavish entitlement programs. Trump has made it clear that he doesn't view Russia as a threat to the United States. A simple interpretation of these dynamics suggests Trump likes Putin. Maybe... or maybe not. I don't want to suggest I have any understanding of the motivations driving Trump's actions, but is it possible there might be a more strategic rationale to the seemingly pro-Putin stance?
**Could the warming of relations with Russia lead to a Kissinger-esque splitting of the Sino-Russian alliance?** Might this be a reason [President Xi recently felt the need to affirm China's "no limits" friendship with Russia](https://substack.com/redirect/3856a4df-62fc-49fb-9796-881bd9f6f316?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)? If containment of the CCP is an objective, a US-Russia alliance would help with that goal. As Mark Twain is reputed to have said, "History doesn't repeat itself, but it does often rhyme."
Despite wild claims that accuse America of becoming both imperialist and isolationist, neither is true. The administration's recent statements reflect a middle ground, focused on retreating from distant foreign entanglements while refocusing on and strengthening the Western Hemisphere, a policy that may soon be known as the Trump Doctrine.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..vrWpIez0oFfC9aiGNYxjctYjMirR_W6Tf9IGLXmvdzM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=157958208)
If my interpretation of developments so far proves true, look for U.S. foreign policy to shift from East and West to North and South. The U.S. will pivot from Europe and the far reaches of the Pacific to the Americas and the Arctic. Every foreign policy discussion will start by asking about U.S. interests, and every deal with, "What do we get out of it?" The key political issues in America will switch to balancing trade relationships, stemming the flow of illegal immigrants and drugs into the U.S., and keeping adversaries such as China out of our backyard. A War on Cartels might replace the War on Terror. Policy will not be dictated by ideology but instead by dollars and cents. Far from imperialist, it is an attempt at avoid the imperial overreach that has doomed great powers in the past. Whereas the first [Monroe Doctrine (and its corresponding Roosevelt Corollary)](https://substack.com/redirect/6bc0e76e-4904-4dec-af07-bf07b304f607?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) signaled American expansion, the second signals a return to our national interests.
The rest of the world may very well have to learn to fend for itself.

clean_body: | Hi Peter, As Donald Trump and an unelected billionaire wreak havoc on our government, one of the most frequently asked (and rightfully so) questions we get is: what are Democrats doing about it? I wanted to make sure I told you exactly what we’re doing to fight back. 🌵After hosting virtual town halls that drew thousands of Arizonans, we hosted our first in-person town hall in Maryvale this week. We heard directly the concerns of the residents of Arizona’s Third and had immigration lawyers and resources available so that Arizonans know how to protect themselves and their rights. 📢 We’ve rallied outside of places like the EPA and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to show solidarity with the employees who were unjustly and unfairly laid off and to make it clear where we stand on Elon Musk’s illegal assault on our democracy. 🧑⚖️ Through my work on the House Oversight Committee, I’ve requested information from leaders within the Trump Administration, including AG Pam Bondi and the Treasury's Inspector General, and have managed to slow down this unprecedented and corrupt attack on taxpayers and our public services. We’re using every tool in our toolbelt to block this extreme right-wing agenda, but I can’t lie, Peter — this work puts us directly in the pathway of Elon Musk and his wealthy campaign coffers.= If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = I won’t let Elon and his campaign spending scare me from doing this work, Peter. # **Trump’s Hypocrisy on Free Speech Is on Full Display**
---
| [](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wlp6f-v9vj3i-kyd76rh5/)
---
| | | | Dear friend, Donald Trump loves to claim he's a champion of free speech—until it applies to the press holding him accountable. Now, his White House is seizing control over which news outlets can cover him up close, a direct attack on the First Amendment and a **shocking break from over a century of tradition.** For all of Trump’s cries about "cancel culture," he has no problem silencing journalists who refuse to bend to his propaganda. His administration is **barring the Associated Press** from key presidential events simply because they won’t adopt his absurd demand to rename the Gulf of Mexico. And now, Trump is **handpicking which outlets get access to the Oval Office and Air Force One,** ensuring only loyalists are allowed in. This is what authoritarianism looks like. **A free press exists to hold power accountable—not to be controlled by it.** Yet, Trump’s hypocrisy knows no bounds, and the corporate media is once again failing to sound the alarm. If Trump gets away with this now, what’s next? **Censorship of all critical media? Persecution of journalists who don’t fall in line?** This is about more than politics—this is about the survival of democracy itself. [**_We cannot sit back and watch Trump dismantle the foundations of our country. The hypocrisy is disgusting, as the MAGA world attacks "woke culture," they themselves are demolishing the first amendment by choosing which press members are allowed to be in the press conference room. Join the fight today to stop him before it’s too late._**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2wlp6f-v9vj3j-kyd76rh6/) In Solidarity, The No Dem Left Behind Team

| Peter, it’s Mondaire Jones. I’m here to tell you about my good friend, Beth Davidson, who is running for Congress in New York’s 17th District. [Beth is our best chance at flipping this district from red to blue. Before I continue, can I count on you to help Beth kickstart her campaign and defeat Mike Lawler in 2026?](https://default.salsalabs.org/T24eadfd9-63c1-4452-a919-478d62c52482/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

| Listen, right now, our current Congressman, Mike Lawler, is failing to address the real needs of the Hudson Valley. He’s too focused on playing party politics with Speaker Mike Johnson and MAGA extremists rather than addressing rising costs and our health care crisis. But Beth has a history of fighting for this community and working across the aisle to get things done. As a former school board leader and now as a County Legislator in Rockland County, she’s worked to lower housing costs, pass common sense gun safety measures, and address our climate crisis. Beth knows this community, and she knows how to win in the Hudson Valley, but she can’t do it alone. This race is going to be one of the most competitive and most expensive in the country. It’s the key to Democrats taking back the House Majority and ending the MAGA Republican trifecta in Washington. Republicans have one of the smallest majorities in history, so we can’t let up for even a moment!! We need to flip this seat and take back the House. [So, can I count on you to support Beth’s campaign today with a contribution split between her campaign and Blue Amp Action?](https://default.salsalabs.org/T5a8f3767-8b0d-450a-84f0-6a0df2c7f867/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

Hi Derek, Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen here — my colleague Chrissy Houlahan said I could reach out.
This week, I traveled across the country with my newborn son to vote against the GOP’s outrageous plan to rip away health care from millions of kids, seniors, pregnant women, and so many more — all so they can give tax breaks to their billionaire donors and friends.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/102896720/530601222/-833980869?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1100-bu-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NDkxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMzk0NjBmMy0zYWY1LWVmMTEtOTBjYi0wMDIyNDgyYTk0ZjQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=m1NcDwu4p1RXfEiV1lHl6l-HmqD1nlg8IwW4gNL6jmg=)
Republican Leadership blocked my ability to vote remotely after giving birth to my son, Sam. It’s outrageous that they would force new parents to choose between caring for our newborn and representing our constituents — but absolutely nothing could stand in my way from being in the Capitol to vote against their cruel and dangerous bill.
You better believe that I’ll be there — no matter how challenging it might be — when Republicans are trying to strip away critical programs like Medicaid and SNAP.
**That’s why I voted against the GOP’s plan to rip away health care, take food off of people’s tables, and make life more expensive for hardworking families — all so they can hand out trillions of dollars to billionaires and wealthy corporations.**
Derek, I promised that I would fight every day for regular families — and I’ll always be there to hold Republicans accountable when they’re hurting hardworking people.
No matter what is thrown our way, I will do what’s right for the American people — but I could really use some support at this moment, because we know this won’t be the last of their attacks.

Hi Peter,

Here at EMILYs List, our top priority this year is to help EMILYs List candidates build the strongest campaigns possible. That's why we want to know: **which races are our supporters most excited about? **

Across the country, brilliant and dedicated women are considering running for office. Many know the challenges they'll face: opposition from deep-pocketed extremists, attacks on their character, insidious double standards, and a political landscape that often sidelines women. But what they may not realize yet is that they have _an entire movement_ standing behind them.

[**We strive to uplift women in races nationwide, but we can't be everywhere at once — and that's why your voice matters. We want to know: Which races are you most excited about? body:
They want the focus to be on their theatrics so that it won’t be on the issues I laid out in my speech.
#
Hi Friend, it’s Congresswoman Sarah McBride — Mandela Barnes and The Long Run said I could reach out to you about something important.
You may have heard that I recently gave my first speech as Delaware’s Congresswoman on the floor of the House of Representatives. And you may have also heard that the Republican who recognized me when I came to the podium used the moment to refer to me as the “Gentleman” from Delaware, “Mr. McBride.” A thoroughly unoriginal schoolyard taunt against trans people.
In truth, they want the focus to be on their theatrics so that it won’t be on the issues I laid out in my speech: the MAGA effort to gut our government at the expense of working people and my focus on bringing down costs and building a government that respects everyone.
Really, their attacks are about more than just me. The truth is they are using trans people as a pawn in their scheme to gut the federal government and line the pockets of Donald Trump’s best friends.
**But I refuse to be a pawn. I refuse to give them that power. And I refuse to let them get away with it.**
That’s why I’m going to spend every day fighting against their attempts to dismantle the federal government, and fighting _for_ the things Delawareans elected me for — regardless of what kind of personal insults Republicans want to throw my way.
Republicans know what they’re doing right now is unpopular, and that’s why they’re desperate to change the conversation. It’s up to us to make sure they don’t get away with it.
[**Friend, if you’re with me, The Long Run and I could really use your support at this moment. AP: Federal appeals court deals a blow to Voting Rights Act, ruling that private plaintiffs can’t sue
Folks,
As we assess threats with Trump back in office, this ruling by the federal 8th Circuit stands out like a sore thumb. It's one of the most dangerous anti-voter rulings we’ve seen in years .
If you missed the details, the impact is pretty simple to understand: In the eight states impacted by the ruling, voters and voting rights organizations can no longer sue to overturn unjust laws under the Voting Rights Act. According to the 8th Circuit, only the Department of Justice (DoJ) has the legal standing to sue states over voting laws.
With former Florida AG Pam Bondi confirmed as Attorney General as a"big lie" spreading MAGA acolyte, do any of us really think that the DOJ is going to protect voting rights over the next four years?
Team, we have to fight this ruling and make sure voters and advocacy groups have the right to defend voting rights in court. Please pitch in $25 or whatever you can to make every vote count, either at the ballot box or in court >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/Z31SNww9Q0CZWIdx46cuSQ2]

Be fierce,
Deb

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: I’m giving the State of the Union Response
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
I'm looking forward to leveling with the American people about what is actually happening in this country.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2247%2E135344%2ED-fFec)

Every year after the State of the Union Address, the opposing political party selects one person to give an official response carried on national television and watched by millions of people.
This year, I've been asked to give that response. It’s a big honor, especially as a brand new, 8-weeks-in Senator.

body:
Take action today to defend our community! | | | Peter, If you were suddenly abducted from your community and the life you know, who would be the first person you’d want to call? Now, imagine stepping off a plane into a place you’ve never seen before but have only heard the most heartbreaking and alarming stories about — **all without knowing when you’d be able to see or hear from the people you love the most again.** **This is the reality Trump has created for hundreds of immigrants who have been detained and sent to Guantanamo Bay in his first month in office.** As Trump delivers on his promise to open a detention facility in Guantanamo Bay to house over 30,000 immigrants, Congress must meet this moment with the urgency it requires! From families reporting they only found out about their loved ones’ abduction to Guantanamo from blurry pictures on social media to an ongoing lawsuit against the Trump administration — it’s alarming how little we know about the conditions our friends, neighbors, and members of our community are facing in this detention center. **What we do know is the long history of abuse, torture interrogation practices, and human rights violations in Guantanamo Bay.** That’s why we cannot sit by and let Trump continue acting in the dark, building up the infrastructure to abduct, kidnap, and tear our communities apart — all while shielded from Congressional oversight and U.S. law. clean_body: Take action today to defend our community! | | | Peter, If you were suddenly abducted from your community and the life you know, who would be the first person you’d want to call? Now, imagine stepping off a plane into a place you’ve never seen before but have only heard the most heartbreaking and alarming stories about — all without knowing when you’d be able to see or hear from the people you love the most again. This is the reality Trump has created for hundreds of immigrants who have been detained and sent to Guantanamo Bay in his first month in office. As Trump delivers on his promise to open a detention facility in Guantanamo Bay to house over 30,000 immigrants, Congress must meet this moment with the urgency it requires! From families reporting they only found out about their loved ones’ abduction to Guantanamo from blurry pictures on social media to an ongoing lawsuit against the Trump administration — it’s alarming how little we know about the conditions our friends, neighbors, and members of our community are facing in this detention center. What we do know is the long history of abuse, torture interrogation practices, and human rights violations in Guantanamo Bay. That’s why we cannot sit by and let Trump continue acting in the dark, building up the infrastructure to abduct, kidnap, and tear our communities apart — all while shielded from Congressional oversight and U.S. law. Can we count on you to defend our communities against Trump’s plans to abduct and detain immigrants thousands and thousands of miles away? Sign our petition to demand Congress shut down the detention camp at Guantanamo Bay once and for all! Peter, this is another move from the Trump administration to incite fear in our communities. By villainizing immigrants and spreading lies about our community, Trump wants to send a deceitful message to the American people. 📣 But our communities have a stronger message to share: We’re unafraid and ready to defend our immigrant neighbors, friends, and loved ones who need us most right now! In solidarity, Juliana and the rest of the United We Dream team | Follow us on: | | | | |

Here's how:

* **Disruption:** Pacaso transforms underutilized vacation properties into fully utilized, co-owned assets. They've facilitated $1B+ in transactions and earned [$100M+ in gross profits.](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx8kD2P4yAQQH8N7mzBgA0uKE6K0uXaK60xDDGSsZEhuey_Xzm72nLb9540H_9u0w3jGrf7X0xk6yvskycfHVbyE4cWdAv9pBpvZ-5H0ZAVWvHBaKNEs9ggUBovvMMh0NwbCFKNZgx-UG7ug2qiBQ49B9DAxQim6wm0U9TPg0PlFTDFyce6H11dqNILS1g_9icdndtTs9ql1lyY_MPgyuAatyeV2mV0WPazOLG8Pmqayv44HDF5oYRxZTCcMJGPj8TkJWP0bcajbnSUJeZv7zBljPftXfxIYXgrR_N1_yS47o2U3PCxOazP_-O6xjJopvj9HPVetP7yu6eFzwAAAP__vABytQ)
* **Ecosystem:** Pacaso's digital marketplace allows buyers to seamlessly co-own, sell, and finance shares of luxury homes while managing scheduling, maintenance, and design.
* **Opportunity:** Until midnight, Pacaso is offering investors the chance to capitalize on this fast-growing co-ownership model for just $2.70/share.

And on the back of impressive first-half earnings that saw the company grow adjusted gross profits by 38%, Pacaso is now focused on international expansion. clean_body: Share your favorite recipe with us and help us create the Grammy Grizzlies America 250 Celebration Cookbook! If you are having trouble viewing this email click here to view in your browser. [] [] [] Join The Grammy Grizzlies Culinary Adventure Share Your Favorite Recipes! On July 4, 2026, the United States of America will commemorate and celebrate the 250th Anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, and Moms for America's Grammy Grizzlies are collecting favorite recipes from around America! The Grammy Grizzlies America 250 Celebration Cookbook Join us in celebrating this monumental moment in American history by sharing the flavors that define your family and community. We invite you to contribute your cherished recipes that have been passed down through generations. We're looking for recipes that showcase America’s diverse heritage. Whether you’re sharing a holiday classic, or a beloved dish enjoyed at family gatherings, we also want to hear the stories that make your recipe special. Be sure to capture the joy of cooking your special recipe, by sharing photos of the preparation and the final creation, and feel free to include a treasured family photo too! Recipe Submission Form [] [] [] Join the Grammy Grizzlies in a heartwarming celebration of community as we gather to share delicious meals and cherished moments, honoring the spirit of togetherness in this special year when we mark America’s 250th Anniversary; let’s create lasting memories through the joy of food and fellowship, reflecting on our rich history and the values that unite us all. Dear Fellow American,

I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future.

A movement is growing, led by progressives—but supported by many well-meaning Americans—to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6de9p1ngni1tf86046akv0phwlzc5v69edyo5n12f247ch5ssrp1atbsh0qo9lu0anu9dvomrfi40ctq4xqddsff9oe3hehrjlupw6mpb4q9t14rtia218khc7vpvvt9swv3kvhkyqfvpxhk7ic5o&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssd0c2&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssd0c2&__onlt=t

Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?

YES
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssd0c2&__onlt=t

NO
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssd0c2&__onlt=t

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6de9p1ngni1tf86046akv0phx9mexck7zvvvx07ss8sfxbs6q5waga8jp6jrls3rc7ro3vhcmivko2x3lqvhz3s301aigbfcji98r0eqnsgmlo24akx5zhktliszt0mf0iefnooxy9h933x1ugqx1&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssd0c2&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=ssd0c2&__onlt=t

And after you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since 1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty." Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans.

The support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention—and for your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

President, Hillsdale College

Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

body:
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/102908116/530633853/623074613?refcode=jtk1394-ot-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWJhNGI5ZDItNGRmNS1lZjExLTkwY2ItMDAyMjQ4MmE5NGY0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=A4Iug8sUqAhNihOI4HYPKZiGZ5DzzO1AR7XoHID6mIw=&emci=a0e45ec1-22f5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&emdi=aba4b9d2-4df5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&ceid=9329426)

Friend,

We knew this was coming with the election of Donald Trump. Mass firings have swept through nearly the entire federal government. Not even our military, which has a history of being apolitical, has been spared.

The very top of our military leadership is being purged for perceived insufficient loyalty to Trump. The chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff – dismissed. The chief of the U.S. Navy – dismissed. The chief of the U.S. Coast Guard – dismissed. The list goes on and on, demonstrating that leaders who have dedicated their lives to serving our nation and keeping us safe are not safe from Musk’s and Trump's personal vendettas.
I’ve been speaking out against these reckless cuts, and I’m continuing to look out for our veterans, as well. They – and we – are increasingly at risk. We all deserve better.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/102908118/530633857/-559624034?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1394-ot-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWJhNGI5ZDItNGRmNS1lZjExLTkwY2ItMDAyMjQ4MmE5NGY0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=A4Iug8sUqAhNihOI4HYPKZiGZ5DzzO1AR7XoHID6mIw=)
Not even military veterans within our nation's civil service have been spared by Trump and Musk. Bear in mind that military veterans make up fully one third of our civil service. In addition to the thousands of terminations across other departments, the thousands of Department of Veterans Affairs employees who have been “cut” are people who not only served our country but also carry out critical work at the department supporting veterans, including combatting veteran suicide.

These poorly-planned and ill-considered firings come as the Department of Veterans Affairs is already facing critical staffing shortages and increased demand for services. To cut such a large number of talented and dedicated civil servants – in whom we have invested years of training, and many of whom had exemplary performance records and superior work experience in government service – demonstrates yet again how little Trump and Musk care about ordinary Americans and how little they understand best practices in managing and governing. These are just “keystrokes” on some minion’s laptop to them. The service these American heroes have given to their country counts for nothing.
**I am committed to aiding veterans and putting their needs first. That's why, as the ranking member of the U.S. Senate Committee on Veterans' Affairs, I just led a group of 35 Democratic Senators demanding Department of Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins immediately reinstate the employees terminated last week.**
**To politicize our military is a disgrace. To terminate our nation's veterans whose service is exemplary is a disgrace. And I will continue to fight the administration's disgraceful, damaging behavior every step of the way.**

Sincerely,

Dick

subject: Let’s restore good governance.

body:
When Trump ran for office, he promised to lower costs and improve lives. He’s doing anything but that.
Peter – look:

When Trump ran for office, he promised to make Americans' lives better by lowering costs and improving the economy.

But instead of focusing on the real needs of everyday Americans, he’s prioritized his own interests – _and Washington has become more divided and chaotic than ever._

We’re seeing a government more obsessed with personal grievances and political retribution than with working to lower costs or solve any problems facing Americans.

Americans deserve elected leaders who will stay focused on delivering for their constituents – **not just work for special interests or their own political survival.** We need leadership that focuses on lowering costs, making healthcare affordable, supporting education, and rebuilding trust in our institutions. Instead we have a budget bill that would cut Medicaid by $880 billion, a bill that would allow banks to increase overdraft fees on their customers, and threatened tariffs on Canada and Mexico that will increase the cost of food and fuel.

In Kentucky, we’ve proven that when we focus on what matters to voters, we can win—even in the toughest political environments. We can build a movement that cuts through the partisan noise and hatred, brings people together, and delivers results. We have the roadmap. We’ve done it before. **And with your help, we can help good people and good candidates do it all across the country.**

Good governance means being honest, transparent, and committed to doing the right thing, regardless of politics. It means tackling the challenges we face together. [**Will you chip in today to help us restore good governance in Washington? clean_body: When Trump ran for office, he promised to lower costs and improve lives. He’s doing anything but that. Peter – look: When Trump ran for office, he promised to make Americans' lives better by lowering costs and improving the economy. But instead of focusing on the real needs of everyday Americans, he’s prioritized his own interests – and Washington has become more divided and chaotic than ever. We’re seeing a government more obsessed with personal grievances and political retribution than with working to lower costs or solve any problems facing Americans. Americans deserve elected leaders who will stay focused on delivering for their constituents – not just work for special interests or their own political survival. We need leadership that focuses on lowering costs, making healthcare affordable, supporting education, and rebuilding trust in our institutions. Instead we have a budget bill that would cut Medicaid by $880 billion, a bill that would allow banks to increase overdraft fees on their customers, and threatened tariffs on Canada and Mexico that will increase the cost of food and fuel. In Kentucky, we’ve proven that when we focus on what matters to voters, we can win—even in the toughest political environments. name: Mark Kelly
subject: This is no way to run the greatest nation on earth
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
If this continues from the top down under President Trump and Elon, millions more people will suffer. That’s the truth.
#

Team — I’m beginning to think these guys don’t actually know what they’re doing!
(That was sarcasm)
Over the weekend, Elon Musk sent out an email to every single federal employee telling them to give five bullet points on what they did in the last week, or be fired. Now, he doesn’t have the authority to do that, but that’s another topic for a separate discussion.
That order fell apart immediately. Some department heads told staff to comply. Some told them not to comply. President Trump told them to comply. The Office of Personnel Management — the actual federal office that manages federal employees — told staff not to comply.
It’s a mess.
I come from the Navy, and I was stationed on the USS Midway. That ship carried around 4000 Sailors and Marines at full capacity. It took a massive amount of coordination and expertise to stay on mission, launch and return aircraft, run the engines, and keep everyone fed, healthy, and in fighting shape.
The federal government is about 2 million people, and they serve about 340 million Americans. They are health care providers, they work on infrastructure, national security, environmental protection, energy. It is an immensely complicated operation of critical importance, and these staff face indiscriminate layoffs, program cuts, and conflicting orders.
If this kind of thing happened in the Navy, Sailors and Marines could get hurt or killed.
If this continues from the top down under President Trump and Elon, millions more people will suffer. That’s the truth.
Republicans in the House and Senate are working to muscle through their budget right now. They’re going to try to codify what President Trump and Elon are doing through the federal budget process. They want to cut hundreds of billions of dollars from Medicaid, food support, and other essential programs to pass trillions in tax breaks for rich people.
I am going to do whatever I can to stop them.
I need you with me.
If you can, please: [**Make a donation to my campaign and help us keep up the fight.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-feb25/.w4QhX4&refcode=em250227-1-f&t=1&akid=5979%2E6688874%2ESm6aqT)

I’ve always had a thing for rebellion. Every movement that has ever changed the world — from civil rights to women’s liberation to climate justice — started because people refused to stay quiet. They didn’t wait for permission. They didn’t let fear or doubt stop them. They acted. That rebellious spirit is what’s needed right now. Because let’s be real — the news under the Trump administration is a never-ending barrage of chaos. Climate disasters, billionaires influencing our democracy, politicians gutting our rights. It’s enough to make anyone feel small. But here’s what I’ve learned after decades of fighting: The feeling of being small is exactly what they want. They want us to believe we’re powerless. They want us hopeless. But we won’t give them that satisfaction. We don’t need to be the biggest, the loudest, or the best. We just need to keep showing up. Because every time we raise our voices and refuse to back down — we prove we are not powerless. **That’s why I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. To take the spirit of rebellion into the halls of power — by resisting the fossil fuel industry’s influence and electing climate champions who will fight for our future, not corporate profits.** But this work takes resources. **[If you believe, like I do, that rebellion is as necessary now as it’s ever been, please contribute whatever you can to keep that spirit burning in the climate movement.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/102909499/530638331/2105508926?refcode=ea.e5fcb2fb-50f5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&ms=ea.e5fcb2fb-50f5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImU1ZmNiMmZiLTUwZjUtZWYxMS05MGNiLTAwMjI0ODJhOTRmNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=7MAw_03l5NAg6d5G387QPzzP1n0oW5YOAiD9-EjCGMU=)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | [**DONATE $5**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/102909500/530638333/2105508926?express_lane=true&amount=5&refcode=ea.e5fcb2fb-50f5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&ms=ea.e5fcb2fb-50f5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImU1ZmNiMmZiLTUwZjUtZWYxMS05MGNiLTAwMjI0ODJhOTRmNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=7MAw_03l5NAg6d5G387QPzzP1n0oW5YOAiD9-EjCGMU=) | [**DONATE $25**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/102909501/530638335/2105508926?express_lane=true&amount=25&refcode=ea.e5fcb2fb-50f5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&ms=ea.e5fcb2fb-50f5-ef11-90cb-0022482a94f4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImU1ZmNiMmZiLTUwZjUtZWYxMS05MGNiLTAwMjI0ODJhOTRmNCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=7MAw_03l5NAg6d5G387QPzzP1n0oW5YOAiD9-EjCGMU=)

clean_body: We’ve got work to do. | I’ve always had a thing for rebellion. Every movement that has ever changed the world — from civil rights to women’s liberation to climate justice — started because people refused to stay quiet. They didn’t wait for permission. They didn’t let fear or doubt stop them. They acted. That rebellious spirit is what’s needed right now. Because let’s be real — the news under the Trump administration is a never-ending barrage of chaos. Climate disasters, billionaires influencing our democracy, politicians gutting our rights. It’s enough to make anyone feel small. But here’s what I’ve learned after decades of fighting: The feeling of being small is exactly what they want. They want us to believe we’re powerless. They want us hopeless. But we won’t give them that satisfaction. We don’t need to be the biggest, the loudest, or the best. We just need to keep showing up. Because every time we raise our voices and refuse to back down — we prove we are not powerless. That’s why I started the Jane Fonda Climate PAC. To take the spirit of rebellion into the halls of power — by resisting the fossil fuel industry’s influence and electing climate champions who will fight for our future, not corporate profits. Tuesday night, all but one Republican House member voted for the largest Medicaid cut in history.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20250227-4802-footer&t=1&akid=4802%2E420207%2E7242H4)
Peter,
On Tuesday night, all but one Republican House member voted for the largest Medicaid cut in history — a vote to strip health care from _millions_ of Americans, including many of their own constituents.
And they’re doing it all so they can fund giant tax breaks for billionaires like Elon Musk and the giant corporations they own.
This Republican Party works only for the 1%, and Democrats cannot be complicit in any part of their harmful agenda. So I’m proud that House Democrats stood together and voted _against_ the MAGA budget.
**Peter, I will never stop fighting for EVERY poor and working person in Seattle and across the country — but I can’t do it without your support.[With our end-of-month deadline coming up, will you pitch in $3 now to help us reach our $40,000 February goal?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20250227-1?refcode=em20250227-4802&amount=3&refcode2=4802_420207_7242H4&akid=4802%2E420207%2E7242H4)**
Trump thinks he can get away with this, but the American people see what he and Musk are doing, and public opinion is starting to turn against them.
By shining a light on their billionaire-first agenda, we can pressure at least some Republicans into standing up for their constituents.
And in the long term, we must continue to build our progressive movement into an enduring electoral force that can defeat MAGA in the next elections.
**That’s where you come in, Peter.** I don’t take a cent from corporations or their PACs. So with our February deadline coming up, I’m counting on your support to reach our $40,000 goal for this month.
[**If you’re with me in the fight for a government that serves _all_ people, not just the wealthiest few, will you pitch in $3 today to support my campaign?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pj-email-20250227-1?refcode=em20250227-4802&amount=3&refcode2=4802_420207_7242H4&akid=4802%2E420207%2E7242H4)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/148be97c-2e9f-4a98-9f81-5825c3345c56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A carton of a dozen eggs, with two eggs cracked and in glass dishes. Image by Candice Bell, Licensed through Shuttertock
Ya know what? Forget the eggs. If I never eat another egg sunny-side or scrambled, omelette or poached...If I never have another egg and cheese on a roll from a New York City bodega...If I never again have another fancy crepe or souffle...all of that can go away and I'll be OK.
Just give me back my country.
### Trump tramples on our democracy
It's been a month and a week since Donald J Trump became President of the United States for a second term. Since that time, Trump and his biggest campaign donor, Elon Musk, have wreaked havoc on virtually every aspect of modern life, both domestic and abroad. They have ignored court orders. They have violated the norms of checks and balances. Trump has offended our allies and forged new coalitions with global leaders we previously considered hostile.
Trump's cabinet appointees cause our food supply to be vulnerable to disease or other safety compromises.
Our national security is at risk to a degree that we probably cannot even fathom.
Our military has been summarily slashed, with untold institutional and strategic knowledge shelved due to disdain for race, gender, or sexuality.
Our nation's most vulnerable are at risk of losing health insurance and vital medication.
Our veterans have lost a suicide prevention hotline, and [potentially thousands of health care workers if we can figure out who was fired and then un-fired. ](https://substack.com/redirect/3bdcdda2-dd2d-4dc3-b043-1ca907d78d1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Our USAID teams that provide valuable soft power abroad through health, infrastructure, social, and educational programs have been shuttered leaving aid recipients to literally die and our own American staffers stranded abroad.
Our national treasury has been invaded and consumer data compromised.
Our federal Department of Education has been decimated. This would be great if it meant student loan forgiveness, but it seems like it really just means that kids with disabilities will not get their IEP needs met.
### There is precedent for this type of power grab
Between January and October of 1933, Adolf Hitler rose to power as chancellor of a coalition government with members of the Nazi party holding only 1⁄3 of the seats in the Reichstag. The following month, the Reichstag was destroyed by fire, triggering a General election. By April of 1933 The Enabling Act made Hitler and his cabinet absolute authorities while individual German states lost power. (Reminder of the ongoing power play in New York state over congestion pricing and in New York City over the dismissal of Mayor Eric Adams' corruption charges.)
In May, 1933, trade unions and other political parties, along with strikes were made illegal. And by October 1933 - only ten months after being legally elected, Hitler withdrew Germany from the League of Nations, tripled the German Army, and ignored any agreements made in the Treaty of Versailles regarding limitations on arms. (Refer to [Open Source](https://substack.com/redirect/d1ce201e-7f42-4507-9ae5-73ae66ef3668?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
Trump's grab at authoritarian power is with historical precedent, and none of it is good.
### "Roll over and play dead" my a$$, James Carville
I am horrified at the suggestion by James Carville that Democrats should "[roll over and play dead.](https://substack.com/redirect/c24490de-c872-480a-9add-9c4d1eec65cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" Easy for Carville to say. As a fellow native Louisianian, I am all-too-familiar with his "laissez les bon temps roullez" roots (translation: "let the good times roll") that let the nation elect Ronald Reagan twice and a series of Bush brush fires burn through the country while Democrats corporatized their strategies and lost their identity as the party of the working class. No thank you, Mr. Carville. Your plan will irreparably damage our country and at your age, you will not live long enough to see us recover.
I ask: where are the real patriots, willing to resist?
### Meanwhile...
Meanwhile, while aging pundits like Carville encourage us to "roll over and play dead", I am positively sickened by the country I am leaving to my 30-something-year-old daughter and other young Americans. They have never known an even quasi-functioning government. (I have vivid memories of her, as an infant, crawling around on a blanket as we watched Operation Desert Storm; eleven years later, of having to explain why the father of a close friend was sent off to war in Afghanistan after the Sept 11 attacks; of her as a young person realizing that the 2008 global economic crash would result in favorite small businesses to close forever; of crushing university tuition and insurmountable student loans, lack of affordable housing, lack of healthcare, lack of livable wages...No - on so many levels, this government has not done right for her generation or those who have come after her. Donald Trump is the apex of a system gone awry since the 1970s.)
Roll over and play dead, my a$$, James Carville.
### **But what can we do? Waiting for MAGA voters to gain sanity in the upcoming Special Elections and Midterms does not seem realistic.**
Until November 2024 I was a firm believer in honoring the will of the people in elections. But at this point, I don't think we can rely on Special Elections and midterms.
The reality is, the involvement of big money and possible technological manipulation makes the prospect of fair elections unrealistic for the foreseeable future. (See [this article](https://substack.com/redirect/f8b5569b-717a-472d-9bd1-da8f525862f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), on the Wisconsin Supreme Court election.) Despite reassurances from federal officials that the 2024 election was safe, Trump continues to dangle a conspiracy that Musk manipulated machines through Starlink. (Refer to [Daily Beast article by Kimmins, Jan 20 2025, "Trump makes odd remark"](https://substack.com/redirect/334a91cd-6152-46c3-90d9-49c5c4b2676a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) Is Trump so addled that he periodically riffs on his malfeasance? Or is he saying he and Musk manipulated the election to instill fear and fealty among his followers? We may never know the truth.
In sum, we may not have an opportunity at a safe and fair election process until we have resoundingly rid ourselves of the America First and MAGA influences.
### But what about the polls that show that MAGA voters are starting to see that Trump does not act in their best interests?
More about those upcoming elections. I don't think we can rely on MAGA supporters to suddenly come to their senses over job losses and economic ruin.
The thought is seductive. But just ask Hillary Clinton about the accuracy of polls. They have been wildly inaccurate for several years now. Therefore, when I hear cheers along the lines of "well NOW his voters will see", I panic that we will do as Carville suggests and "roll over and play dead", all the while waiting for reason to overtake the MAGA voters and bring them to their senses. Take it from Hillary: the polls are just not accurate anymore.
### Trump as the Come Back Kid
The other Clinton -- Bill -- who helped catapult James Carville to political pundit status, was known as the Come Back Kid. Arguably, we have recent experience that establishes Trump has now claimed the title as the most resilient Come Back Kid of modern times. Did you ever think he could even get on a ballot after January 6, 2021? After the E. Jean Carroll verdict? After the 34 felonies? Heck - I never thought he could get on a ballot after the Access Hollywood tape! And yet here we are.
### Here's what I think will happen
My prediction is that Trump and Musk will use the decimation of our federal systems for profit, and to buy time to get a third presidential term ratified. As we get closer to Special Elections, midterms, or the next presidential election, we will see talk of aggressive hiring and restoration of services such as veterans health care or Medicaid.
While the [polls right now show](https://substack.com/redirect/fe2160dc-a509-4b79-8301-1121324327ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Trump supporters are getting shaken by what they are seeing, mark my words, Trump will do something like create a quasi Medicaid system, or re-branded veterans health administration. He and his social media geniuses will dangle it in front of voters just before a Special Election or midterm, all the while convincing them that Elon did wonders to advance the America First policies and clean up fraud and waste in our government. And Elon is such a great guy, he did all of this without so much as drawing a paycheck. I can hear it now. Make America Grift Again.
### Law suits
So what should we do? For starters, we should continue with the law suits and the courts for as long as we have them. But this will only last so long, and I believe that time is running out. I have expressed concern on Bluesky and other social media platforms that Trump will soon do like Hitler, and set up an alternative court structure such as the "Volksgerichshof" (Refer to [Holocaust Encyclopedia](https://substack.com/redirect/adef03b9-ba39-44b6-a040-6b4f6e680d0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).) in order to get the judicial results he needs.
Sadly, while we wait for the courts to bring a halt to Trump's destruction, our national security, our food systems, and our public health systems threaten widespread risk that will make the Covid pandemic seem like a bad flu season.
### What else can we do?
Bernie Sanders has embarked on a very brave [Tour to Fight Oligarchy](https://substack.com/redirect/70a34e88-8951-47b2-84ba-4351b6ffb4ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), targeting places that were won by Biden in 2020 but swayed to Republican candidates in 2024. (Sidebar: I gotta say, I was never a Bernie supporter, but now I gotta wonder if there wasn't genuine strength and wisdom in his message.)
An [economic strike is planned for Friday, February 28, 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/dee03d0d-f2d3-4efe-a329-db90971c8e86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), in which consumers are to generate no financial activity for 24 hours.
Daily protests take place in virtually every city and in our nation's capitol.
Are these effective? Emotionally and spiritually, yes. In reality? Probably not. Musk and the Musketeers continue their work, often spending the night in federal buildings in their efforts to perpetrate their coup. I'm not even sure they are aware of how widespread the protests are in multiple cities throughout the country.
Our data is long gone. The first step in reparations will be that we will all need new identification numbers to replace our social security numbers. But I'm getting ahead of myself. Save that for another article on how we rebuild our post-MAGA America.
### We need to think beyond protests, rallies, and law suits.
For now, I welcome the government [shut down contemplated by House Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/b9f8ed55-e3a1-4093-8b42-906fbb4a4465?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I hope that you will join me in keeping pressure on Democrats to not crater to the Republican demands to approve the spending bill without protecting ourselves from the ongoing Musk-induced coup.
As I say that, I am cognizant that such a government shut down may result in the executive office establishing an alternative to Congress. I don't take this proposition lightly. Hitler's 1933 was not really all that long ago.
I have faith in our historic allies, such as our NATO partners, Mexico, and Canada to continue to watch and to provide aid if necessary. And I have hope in our military and recently fired generals to rely on the examples set in other nations. Will it be necessary to act with physical and military force to reclaim our government from this coup?
I leave the question out there. I do not have an answer at this time.
For right now -- forget the price of eggs. We have a country to save.
Buckle up. We are in for some very tough times in the weeks ahead.
_If we haven 't met yet, I am Paula Collins. I ran for Congress in November 2024 in NY-21. I continue to write about life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. Your comments are invaluable to me. Please let me hear from you. _

Just give me back my country. Trump tramples on our democracy It's been a month and a week since Donald J Trump became President of the United States for a second term. Since that time, Trump and his biggest campaign donor, Elon Musk, have wreaked havoc on virtually every aspect of modern life, both domestic and abroad. They have ignored court orders. They have violated the norms of checks and balances. Trump has offended our allies and forged new coalitions with global leaders we previously considered hostile. Trump's cabinet appointees cause our food supply to be vulnerable to disease or other safety compromises. Our national security is at risk to a degree that we probably cannot even fathom. Our military has been summarily slashed, with untold institutional and strategic knowledge shelved due to disdain for race, gender, or sexuality. Our nation's most vulnerable are at risk of losing health insurance and vital medication. Our veterans have lost a suicide prevention hotline, and Our USAID teams that provide valuable soft power abroad through health, infrastructure, social, and educational programs have been shuttered leaving aid recipients to literally die and our own American staffers stranded abroad. Our national treasury has been invaded and consumer data compromised. Our federal Department of Education has been decimated. This would be great if it meant student loan forgiveness, but it seems like it really just means that kids with disabilities will not get their IEP needs met. There is precedent for this type of power grab Between January and October of 1933, Adolf Hitler rose to power as chancellor of a coalition government with members of the Nazi party holding only 1⁄3 of the seats in the Reichstag. The following month, the Reichstag was destroyed by fire, triggering a General election. By April of 1933 The Enabling Act made Hitler and his cabinet absolute authorities while individual German states lost power. (Reminder of the ongoing power play in New York state over congestion pricing and in New York City over the dismissal of Mayor Eric Adams' corruption charges.) In May, 1933, trade unions and other political parties, along with strikes were made illegal. And by October 1933 - only ten months after being legally elected, Hitler withdrew Germany from the League of Nations, tripled the German Army, and ignored any agreements made in the Treaty of Versailles regarding limitations on arms. (Refer to .) Trump's grab at authoritarian power is with historical precedent, and none of it is good. "Roll over and play dead" my a$$, James Carville I am horrified at the suggestion by James Carville that Democrats should "" Easy for Carville to say. As a fellow native Louisianian, I am all-too-familiar with his "laissez les bon temps roullez" roots (translation: "let the good times roll") that let the nation elect Ronald Reagan twice and a series of Bush brush fires burn through the country while Democrats corporatized their strategies and lost their identity as the party of the working class. Meanwhile...
